name: OPA211 / OPA2211
tagline: TI's 1.1 nV/√Hz, 45 MHz bipolar precision amp; Head-Fi rollers found the OPA2211A more open than the LM4562.

lineage.note: Sole source; SBOS377 first dated October 2006, Burr-Brown-style OPA prefix. Enhanced-product OPA211-EP (2012) and OPA2211-EP followed.

27 V/µs; settles 400 ns to 0.01%, 700 ns to 0.0015%
key_specs.condition: ±15 V, G = −1, 10 V step, CL 100 pF

3.6 mA typ, 4.5 mA max; 6 mA max (−40 to +125 °C)
Bipolar, diode-protected (≤10 mA); no phase reversal

reputation.summary: Well regarded for rolling and DAC output stages, on forum impressions rather than measurements. Head-Fi rollers ranked the OPA211 above most parts, including LM/LME chips; one found the OPA2211A 'more open, yet not harsh' than the LM4562. Japanese reviewers find it clearer than the OPA2134 and drier than the OPA627. Shanling retail copy lists it in DAC LPF stages.
typical_uses: DAC differential, summing and low-pass filter stages
Shanling M6 Pro 21 and EM7 LPF (retail copy)
Low-impedance gain stages and ADC drivers (sources below 2 kΩ)
SR560-style LNAs, unity-gain-stable stand-in for OP37/LT1028
caveats: SMD only: the exposed pad 'must be connected to V–', not ground. Check how DIP adapters connect it.
VSSOP/SON singles: pin 8 is Shutdown (active high), never leave it open. The SOIC single's pin 8 is NC.
Rev H (Nov 2015) swapped the SON single's V+ and V− pins; rev I fixed it. Avoid rev H layouts.
Input diodes conduct on large fast steps; the 10 mA limiting resistor adds noise. TI targets sources below 2 kΩ.
Wideband (45 MHz at G = 1): mind capacitive loads and adapter layout. Impressions depend on circuit and genre.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit reports checked yet. No DIP exists: a DIP-8 'OPA2211' is an adapter or remark. Check markings ('OPA 2211 A' DDA, 'OBHQ' SON, 'OPA 211 [A]' SOIC) and that DDA parts have an exposed pad soldered to V−.

refuted_claims: 'Revisions A–F undocumented / no rev G copy' is wrong: copies of revs A, F, G (Mouser) and I were found.
'OPA211-EP datasheet number not found' is wrong: it is SBOS638, June 2012.
'Non-A OPA2211 never released' is too strong: the enhanced-product OPA2211MDRGTEP exists; only a commercial non-A dual is unfound.
